STATE OF RHODE ISLAND 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION 
 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 
Docket No. 25-45-GE (Rhode Island Energy Base Distribution Rate Case) and Docket No. 
25-33-GE (Acceleration of Hold Harmless Commitment) 
 
These matters relate to Rhode Island Energy’s (Company) pending base distribution rate case. On 
November 26, 2025, Rhode Island Energy filed a request to increase electric and gas base 
distribution rates under a proposed two-year rate plan. The request was modified in two additional 
filings on April 16, 2026, and May 11, 2026. Further modifications were made following the 
hearings, as filed on July 31, 2026. As modified, in the first rate year, the Company requested an 
increase of $77.3 million for electric distribution service and approximately $130.3 million for gas 
distribution service. Although the Company filed a two-year rate plan, on August 12, 2026, the 
Commission voted to deny the request for a second rate year increase. 
 
In addition to seeking an increase in distribution rates, the Company also proposed to accelerate 
credits to customers relating to PPL Rhode Island’s acquisition of the Company that took effect in 
May of 2022. The credits have been referred to as “Hold Harmless Credits” because they are 
intended to hold customers harmless from certain tax impacts caused by the acquisition. In that 
filing, the Company proposed to provide credits to customers through fixed bill credits in January, 
February, and March 2027, and 2028. 
 
At 10:00 a.m., the Chairman called the open meeting to order. In attendance were Chairman 
Gerwatowski, Commissioner Anthony, and Commissioner Bradbury. Staff members Todd Bianco, 
Cynthia Wilson-Frias, Esq., Rhianon Small, Ryan Coyne, Esq., Stephanie De La Rosa, and Alan 
Nault were in attendance.  
 
Chairman Gerwatowski explained that the Commission had conducted five prior open meetings 
between August 12, 2026 and August 21, 2026 to deliberate on the issues in these matters and had 
reached consensus on almost all issues. The purpose of this open meeting was to memorialize those 
decisions into formal enforceable motions. All of the prior open meeting deliberations were

During prior deliberations, the PUC identified several items that do not require a motion but will 
require some direction to be provided to the Company in the order. Therefore, a lack of a motion 
on those items should not be taken as abandonment of the concerns raised on those issues. 
 
The following votes were taken.

2 
 
Enterprise Resource Planning - Information Technology Investment – Regulatory Asset 
 
1. Move to reject recovery of information technology Enterprise Resource Planning non-
recurring operations & maintenance expenses that were incurred prior to January 1, 2026. 
Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0 
 
2. Move to approve the creation of a regulatory asset for information technology Enterprise 
Resource Planning non-recurring operations & maintenance expenses. Moved by 
Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0 
 
3. Move to allow the Company to begin booking expenses to the Enterprise Resource 
Planning regulatory asset as of January 1, 2026. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, 
Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0 
 
4. Move to cap the accrual of expenses in the Enterprise Resource Planning regulatory asset 
at $7,975,429, inclusive of the 2026 Actual and Projected Spend through Rate Year 2 
reflected in RR 28-3. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner 
Bradbury. Vote 3-0 
 
5. Move to allow the Enterprise Resource Planning regulatory asset to accrue interest based 
on the average rate over the current calendar year for the 10-year Constant Maturity 
Treasury Bonds and the accrual will not impact the cap. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0 
 
6. Move that expenses booked to the Enterprise Resource Planning regulatory asset will be 
amortized over ten years. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner 
Bradbury. Vote 3-0 
 
7. Move to allow recovery of the first year of amortization of the Enterprise Resource 
Planning regulatory asset in Rate Year 1 based on the forecasted $7,061,848, which 
represents the 2026 Actual and Projected Spend and Rate Year 1 Actual and Projected 
Spend reflected in RR-28-3. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by 
Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0 
 
Customer Information System - Regulatory Asset 
 
8. Move to reject recovery of Customer Information System non-recurring operations & 
maintenance expenses prior to January 1, 2026. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, 
Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0 
 
9. Move to defer a ruling on whether to allow the creation of a regulatory asset for Customer 
Information System non-recurring operations & maintenance expenses to a future docket. 
Expenses incurred commencing January 1, 2026 may be found to be eligible for inclusion 
in a regulatory asset should one be allowed. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded 
by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0

3 
 
 
10. Move to require the Company to file, in a new docket no later than November 1, 2026, a 
comprehensive Customer Information System (CIS) investment plan based on the total 
expenses projected in this proceeding. 
The investment plan shall: 
a. Provide a clear description of the functionalities associated with the total CIS 
spending budget presented in this proceeding. 
b. Clearly explain how the new CIS will resolve all of the billing-related problems 
that were identified in the record of this case, which includes the billing system 
investigation and report and to meet the current statutory and regulatory 
requirements. 
c. Identify any additional functionalities not included in the Company’s prior proposal 
that are necessary to meet the current statutory and regulatory requirements, 
including any such functionalities that would require additional future expenditures 
and associated cost recovery. 
d. Include a timeline the Company will commit to filing with the Commission, at a 
minimum, proposed basic time-of-use rates. 
e. Include the Company’s commitments and timeline for implementing a new billing 
format following CIS implementation, including a specified date by which the new 
billing format will be completed. 
f. Propose performance metrics that ensure customers have access to a consistent 
report of their charges, usage, and account information, regardless of the channel 
through which customers access or pay their bills. 
g. Include performance metrics consistent with, or comparable to those required 
following the Company’s prior transition, as applicable. 
h. Include performance metrics specifically designed to measure the Company’s 
consistency with the Commission-approved rate tariffs, including the accurate 
application of rates, charges, and tariff provisions through the CIS. 
 
Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0 
 
Other/Strategic Information Technology 
 
11. Move to deny the creation of a regulatory asset for Other Strategic Programs non-recurring 
operations and maintenance investments. Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded 
by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
12. Move to allow estimated Rate Year 1 operations and maintenance expense for Other 
Strategic Programs shown on Attachment RR 28-3, lines 17-18, amortized over 3 years 
($2,329,814). Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. 
Vote 3-0. 
 
Software Maintenance 
 
13. Move to allow the Company’s proposed increase to software maintenance as shown in 
SAB-3 OM Summary-R, line 13, column D of $17,790,171 which comprises $9,572,685

4 
 
for electric and $8,217,486 for gas net of any amounts for ongoing Green Button Connect 
Expenses that the Commission denied in Docket 25-19-EL. Moved by Commissioner 
Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
14. Move to require the Company to provide the Division of Public Utilities and Carriers with 
information sufficient such that the Division can confirm that the approximate $700,000 
identified by Witness Pou was not miscategorized as recurring operations and maintenance 
expense. Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 
3-0. 
 
Information Technology Reporting Requirements – Projects greater than $500,000 
 
15. Move that for each major strategic information technology project exceeding $500,000, the 
Company shall provide supporting documentation sufficient for the Division of Public 
Utilities and Carriers to complete its review consistent with its position in this docket. 
Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
16. Move that the Company will work in good faith with the Division to establish the reporting 
requirements. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. 
Vote 3-0. 
 
Facilities 
 
17. Move to deny inclusion of the proposed capital improvement expenses (fit-out costs) for 
the Northwoods Facility in rate base. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
18. Move to allow recovery of the proposed capital improvement expenses (fit-out costs) for 
the Northwoods Facility net of the tenant allowance amortized and recovered over the life 
of the lease without a return. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
19. Move to allow lease expense related to the Northwoods Facility of $935,000 in the Rate 
Year 1 revenue requirement. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
20. Move to reduce the revenue requirement by $73,000 to reflect expected operations and 
maintenance savings from the use of the Northwoods Facility auditorium. Moved by 
Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Legal Expenses 
 
21. Move to reduce the Company’s legal expenses in the proposed electric and gas revenue 
requirement by a total of $440,766. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0.

5 
 
 
Inflation Adjustments 
 
22. Move to reject the Company’s use of a general inflation factor to the Consultants, 
Contractors, and other O&M categories. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by 
Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Grid X Software 
 
23. Move to reject the Company’s request to recover expenses for Grid X software related to 
the development of Time of Use rates. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Rate Case Expense 
 
24. Move to approve rate case expense as filed in PH-2-1, amortized over three years, after 
removing the $132,168 related to Grid X. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by 
Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Depreciation 
 
25. Move to reject the Division’s contingency adjustments included in its calculation of 
depreciation. Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. 
Vote 3-0. 
 
26. Move to adopt the Division’s net salvage value calculations for gas mains and services. 
Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Tata Consulting 
 
27. Move to require the Company to confirm that it normalized out of the Test Year $724,000 
for the Tata IT Metering Support contract related to Project number 70017516 the 
description of which was: “This is a project to ensure the metering system is available for 
RIE”. If not, then the Company shall make the appropriate adjustment to either normalize 
out the expense or show that it is only including the incremental difference between that 
contract and any Rate Year contract providing ongoing support for the metering system. 
The Company shall provide the confirmation and highlight the associated values in the 
Compliance Filings. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner 
Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Uncollectible Factors 
 
28. Move to reject the Company’s proposed changes to the uncollectible factors for purposes 
of calculating the gas and electric revenue requirements. Moved by Chairman 
Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0.

6 
 
Vacancy Rate 
 
29. Move to accept the Company’s proposal to use a 2.5% labor vacancy rate for the calculation 
of the gas revenue requirement. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
30. Move to accept the Division’s proposal to use a 5.0% labor vacancy rate for the calculation 
of the electric revenue requirement. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
DG Acceleration 
 
31. Move to find that the payments made to the Distributed Generation Developers for the 
Tiverton and Weaver Hill projects at issue in this case should have been made based on an 
in-service date of 2032 instead of the in-service date used by the Company of 2028. The 
result is a total downward adjustment of $2,400,820 to net plant. Moved by Chairman 
Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 2-1 with Commissioner 
Anthony dissenting. She would have used an in-service date of 2035 in lieu of 2032. 
 
Reclosers 
 
32. Move to disallow recovery in the revenue requirement of the cost of the recloser on the 
33F6 circuit that was included in the March 5, 2026, justification memorandum. Moved by 
Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
33. Move that the Company shall propose a Circuit Reliability Mechanism for the circuits 
addressed by the recloser investments approved for recovery in this proceeding. The 
proposed mechanism shall include the following structure, in addition to any other 
elements the Company may propose: 
a. 
The performance target each individual circuit will be the Company’s estimate 
of CKAIFI after recloser installation, inclusive of major storms that circuit, as 
provided in the corresponding circuit justification memos filed in the 
Company’s response to Division 13-22-2.  
b. 
The performance measures will be calculated annually for each circuit 
as follows:   
1. CKAIFI Deviation = (Actual CKAIFI – CKAIFI Performance 
Target). 
2. A CKAIFI Deviation of 0.1 or less shall have no service quality 
adjustment.  
3. A CKAIFI Deviation of 0.5 or greater shall have the 
maximum service quality adjustment.  
4. The maximum service quality adjustment should be equal to the 
annual revenue requirement for the reclosers on the circuit.  
c. 
In addition to this structure, the Company may propose an alternate proposal. 
d. 
The first performance period begins on January 1, 2026.

7 
 
e. 
Circuits will be added to the Accountability Mechanism when the company 
seeks cost recovery for reclosers for the purposes of improving circuit 
reliability.  
f. 
The Company will file an updated Service Quality Plan for Commission 
review and approval in Docket No. 3628. Other parties may seek to intervene 
in Docket No. 3628.  
 
Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Cost of Capital 
 
34. Move to use a capital structure of 52 percent equity and 48 percent debt for purposes of 
calculating the revenue requirement. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by 
Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. The Chairman noted that this represented a reduction 
from the Company’s proposed 57% equity ratio which has a significant impact on the 
return. 
 
35. Move to deny the Company’s request to increase their return on equity to 10.75% and 
instead retain the current return on equity of 9.275%. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, 
Seconded by Commissioner Anthony & Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Gas Decoupling 
 
36. Move to authorize the Company to include growth-related projects that were typically 
excluded under the previous decoupling mechanism in its upcoming Fiscal Year 2028 Gas 
Infrastructure Safety and Reliability proposal, subject to implementation of a total revenue 
decoupling mechanism implemented in the DAC filing for effect November 1, 2028. 
Commissioner. Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. 
Vote 3-0. 
 
37. Move to direct the Company to file a revised gas decoupling proposal by May 1, 2027, 
based on total revenue decoupling across all rate classes, for effect November 1, 2028, 
initially covering the period April 1, 2027, through March 2028. Moved by Commissioner 
Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
C-06 Rate Design 
 
38. Move to limit the volumetric base distribution charge for the C-06 rate class customers to 
the sum of the current base distribution charge plus the current CapEx factor for the C-06 
rate class. Any remaining revenue requirement allocated to the C-06 rate class in the 
revenue requirement shall be allocated to the customer charge, provided, however, the 
resulting customer charge shall not exceed $21, in which case, the remainder would be 
allocated to the volumetric charge. Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by 
Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0.

8 
 
Seasonal 
 
39. Move to direct the Company to implement a seasonal volumetric charge to residential 
electric customers as follows: 
a. There will be two seasons: a winter season comprising December, January, 
February, and March usage and a non-winter season comprising the remaining 
months of the year. 
b. The ratio of the base distribution volumetric charge in the winter season to the non-
winter season shall be equal to the ratio of winter peak to summer peak provided in 
response to PUC 2-2(b). 
c. The maximum difference between the winter season and non-winter season rates 
shall not exceed 1.5 cents per kWh. 
 
Moved by Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Amtrak Settlement 
 
40. Move to approve the Settlement entered into between Rhode Island Energy, Amtrak, the 
Division of Public Utilities and Carriers, Rhode Island Center for Justice, Conservation 
Law Foundation, National Grid LNG, and Walmart resolving Amtrak’s cost of service and 
rate design issue. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner 
Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Cost Allocation and Rate Design 
 
41. Move to approve the Company’s methodology for cost allocation and rate design subject 
to the prior votes on cost allocation and rate design. Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, 
Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Line Extension Policy 
 
42. Move to phase out the line extension construction allowance as included in Gas 101 Tariff, 
Service and Main Extension Policies 1, 2, and 3 over three years commencing April 1, 
2027, such that by April 1, 2029, there will be no construction allowance applied against 
the cost of new service and main extensions. 
a. On April 1, 2027, there will be a 33% reduction to the revenue offset allowance; 
b. On April 1, 2028, there will be a 66% reduction to the revenue offset allowance; 
c. On April 1, 2029, there will be a 100% reduction to the revenue offset allowance. 
d. For residential customers, the intent is that the percentage reductions will apply to 
both the Threshold for CIAC Waiver and revenue offset allowance. 
e. By November 1, 2026, the Company shall file with the PUC a revised Service and 
Main Extension Policy Tariff that includes all eligibility criteria for applications to 
be considered qualified during each phase.  The eligibility criteria should be guided 
by objectively identifiable and reliable information.  Standards could be different 
for residential vs. other projects.

9 
 
f. Consideration should include defining a genuine application; where in the process 
a customer needs to be to qualify for the applicable revenue offset allowance; 
whether the information required becomes more refined in each subsequent 
transition year; and the rules that will apply to a customer/developer’s changes to 
project scope, size, or location, and any other terms and conditions the Company 
identifies as required. 
 
Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Integrated Planning 
 
43. Move to direct Rhode Island Energy to make a supplemental filing in the pending Gas 
Long-Range Resource and Requirements Plan Forecast Period 2026/27 to 2030/31 
proceeding, Docket No. 26-26-NG, by March 1, 2027, addressing three issues: 
a. Demand Forecast Reliability: Provide expert testimony to support the reliability of 
the Company's reliance on the historical data series and modeling approaches that 
underpin the Company’s forecasts, including an assessment of how the 
methodology can be improved.  
b. Planning Consistency: Update the LRP using a methodology supported by 
testimony that ensures consistency between the Company's gas demand forecasts 
and the electrification assumptions used in its electric system planning, including 
assumptions regarding electric heating and other end uses. 
c. Alternative Planning Scenarios: Provide alternative planning scenarios that would 
allow for compliance with the Act on Climate, including, at a minimum, the EC4 
scenarios in the Climate Action Strategy 2025, a scenario with a higher rate of 
adoption of electrification, and a scenario with a lower rate of adoption. The filing 
should provide sufficient quantitative analysis and supporting information to allow 
the Commission and Division to evaluate the Company's forecasts and the 
resilience of its proposed resource plan under these alternative scenarios. 
 
Moved by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Large Load Tariff 
 
44. Move to direct the Company to file an extra-large electric load tariff by December 31, 2026, 
designed to prevent such customers, such as data centers, from, at a minimum, adversely 
affecting grid reliability and resilience, shifting costs to existing customers, or causing 
undue rate shock. The Company should initially define the class minimum demand of 20 
MW or provide testimony supporting a different threshold. Moved by Chairman 
Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Leave on for Landlord 
 
45. Move to direct the Company to compile a list of all enrolled landlords and, with input from 
the Division, develop and file a plan to contact each landlord for confirmation they plan to 
remain in the program together with a recertification process that will take place no less

10 
 
often than every two years. The recertification plan should be incorporated into Section 3.1 
of the General Rules and Regulations Schedule A of the Gas 101 tariff and Electric Terms 
and Conditions. The tariff advice shall be filed by February 28, 2027, for review and 
approval by the Commission. In accordance with the jurisdictional responsibilities, the 
Division will oversee RI Energy’s compliance with the plan once approved. Moved by 
Commissioner Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Low Income Discount Rate 
 
46. Move to direct the Company to update RR-62 as part of its Compliance Filing. The 
Company should then provide the Commission with status updates consistent with its 
workplan, specifically highlighting progress on the CIS implementation and re-tiering of 
customers on November 1, 2026, and December 1, 2026. Any delays or significant 
unexpected challenges should be included in the filings. Moved by Commissioner 
Anthony, Seconded by Commissioner Bradbury. Vote 3-0. 
 
Accelerated Hold Harmless Implementation 
 
47. Move that the Company’s proposal, as filed, to provide miscellaneous bill credits to 
implement PPL Corporation and PPL Rhode Island Holdings, LLC’s obligation to hold 
harmless Rhode Island customers from any changes to Accumulated Deferred Income 
Taxes as a result of the Acquisition of the Company by PPL (“Hold Harmless 
Acceleration Proposal”) is denied; provided, however, that the Commission authorizes 
the Company to implement the proposal with the following modifications and conditions: 
 
a. In calculating the Hold Harmless values to be credited separately to electric and 
gas distribution customers, the Company shall calculate and determine the Hold 
Harmless lump sums (line 9 of Attachment PH 1-1) and the Rate Year 1 Hold 
Harmless Revenue Requirement (line 10 of Attachment PH 1-1) separately for 
electric distribution and gas distribution, as reflected in Attachment PH 1-1, as 
follows: 
i. The Company shall perform the calculation using assumptions and 
methodologies that are consistent with those used to develop the estimates 
under “Scenario 3” provided in Attachment PH 1-1, except that the 
discount rate used to determine the net present value shall be the 12-month 
average of the Bank of America Prime rate, measured from August 2025 
through July 2026; 
ii. For each applicable calculation, the amount calculated for the Rate Year 1 
Hold Harmless Revenue Requirement illustrated on line 10 shall be moved 
from the rate case revenue requirements and be consolidated with the 
applicable lump sum on line 9 (“Consolidated Fixed Hold Harmless 
Credits”); and 
iii. The resulting applicable Consolidated Fixed Hold Harmless Credits shall 
be distributed to electric and gas customers, respectively.

11 
 
b. The Company shall distribute the electric distribution Consolidated Fixed Hold 
Harmless Credit through a uniform fixed monthly bill credit on all electric 
accounts, commencing with bills rendered in October of 2026 and continuing 
through the month of September 2027. The uniform fixed monthly credits on 
electric distribution bills shall expire beginning with the month of October 2027. 
 
c. The Company shall distribute the gas distribution Consolidated Fixed Hold 
Harmless Credit in two parts.  In part one, the Company shall offset any amounts 
owed by gas distribution customers on the deferred gas cost balance as of the end 
of October 2026.  In part two, the Company shall distribute the remaining balance 
of the Consolidated Fixed Hold Harmless Credit through a uniform fixed monthly 
bill credit on all gas distribution accounts, commencing with bills rendered in 
December 2026 through April 2027. The uniform fixed monthly bill credits on 
gas distribution bills shall expire beginning with the month of May 2027. 
 
d. At the end of each of the specified crediting periods (i.e., October-September for 
electric; and December-April for gas), the Company shall reconcile the amounts 
actually credited with the applicable Consolidated Fixed Hold Harmless Credits 
that were calculated in accordance with (a) above.   
 
e. To the extent the electric reconciliation has a positive balance to be provided to 
electric distribution customers, the Company shall make a proposal after 
September 2027 to credit the Company’s storm fund before the end of 2027.  To 
the extent the reconciliation has a negative balance from the Company over-
crediting the electric customers, the Company shall be entitled to recover the 
balance and shall propose a recovery mechanism after the crediting period to 
recover the applicable amount from electric distribution customers. 
 
f. To the extent the gas reconciliation has a positive balance to be provided to gas 
distribution customers, the Company shall make a proposal after April of 2027 to 
credit gas distribution customers before the end of 2027 in the Company’s 
Distribution Adjustment (DAC) filing.  To the extent the reconciliation has a 
negative balance from the Company over-crediting the gas customers, the 
Company shall be entitled to recover the balance and shall propose a recovery 
mechanism to recover the remaining balance from gas distribution customers in 
the DAC. 
 
g. The Company shall notify the Commission by no later than 4:00 pm on August 
25, 2026 whether the Company is agreeing to voluntarily move forward with the 
Hold Harmless Acceleration Proposal as modified by the Commission, or is 
withdrawing its request to implement the acceleration. 
 
h. If the Company elects to withdraw its Hold Harmless Acceleration Proposal, the 
Company is directed to apply an annual Hold Harmless credit relating to its 
federal transmission rates against the Company’s transmission costs for which it 
seeks recovery in each subsequent Retail Rate filing, commencing with the Retail

12 
 
Rate filing made in 2027. In the first filing in 2027, such transmission-related 
credit must also include the balance of any Hold Harmless transmission credits 
accrued as a liability by the Company since the acquisition of Narragansett 
Electric by PPL. 
 
Moved by Chairman Gerwatowski, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Compliance Filing 
 
48. Move to require Rhode Island Energy to submit a compliance filing on or before August 
27, 2026, for effect on usage on and after September 1, 2026. Moved by Chairman 
Gerwatowksi, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 3-0. 
 
Motion to adjourn made by Commissioner Bradbury, Seconded by Commissioner Anthony. Vote 
3-0. 
 
Adjournment at 10:45 a.m.
